title: Woman's haori
medium: Rayon, metallic thread; balanced plain weave with discontinuous supplementary weft patterning, stencil printed warp and weft (heiyo-gasuri meisen); balanced plain weave lining, printed (silk screen)
medium_parts: balanced plain weave with discontinuous supplementary weft patterning, stencil printed warp and weft (heiyo-gasuri meisen)
balanced plain weave lining, printed (silk screen)
identifying_description: Printed designs of Mickey mouse, boys playing soldiers, bunnies, and a ball, mixed with images of a fleet at sea and a military train.
web_text: This haori (kimono-style jacket) offers an example of propaganda in textile form, but subtly; references to the Imperial Japanese agenda appear only on the jacket's lining, where machines of conquest from air, land, and sea punctuate a design that might appear innocuous at first glance. Children march under a Japanese flag, and Mickey Mouse bounds energetically across the scene, alongside a rabbit. However, Mickey Mouse, that mainstay of Western culture, had, from the early 1930s, become a symbol in Japan of the American aggressor, from whom many feared an imminent full-scale invasion of Asia and the South Pacific.
